title: T1597 — Search Closed Sources
subtitle: Watch an operator buy their way to an entry point, while the SOC sees almost nothing.
aria: Animated diagram of an attacker purchasing closed-source data about a target company from a threat intel vendor, a technical data broker, and a credential broker, while the SOC only sees indirect alerts. A written version of every step follows below the diagram.

steps.title: Choose a target
steps.caption: The operator picks a company and lists what to buy: sector context, an external asset map, and employee credentials.
steps.defender: Nothing has touched your network. The only defense at this stage is knowing what outsiders can buy about you.

detection.detail: This activity is not visible to the victim yet.

steps.title: Open a paid vendor account
steps.caption: Using a front-company identity, the operator buys a subscription to a closed threat intel portal.
steps.defender: Vendors screen buyers, but accounts can be bought or stolen. Ask vendors for portal-audit logs and keyword alerts.

steps.title: Search closed reports
steps.caption: Inside the portal the operator searches the company and its sector. Two private reports describe recent changes and the ransomware groups most active in that industry.
steps.defender: Some platforms alert brands when their name is searched. A spike like this is an early, buyable signal.

steps.title: Buy technical data
steps.caption: The operator pays a data-broker API for passive DNS, WHOIS history, and certificate records for the target's domains.
steps.defender: Data platforms log who queries your domains. Bulk lookups about your domain from one client are worth reviewing.

steps.title: Map the attack surface
steps.caption: The purchased records reveal old subdomains, an expired certificate, and a legacy VPN portal that still resolves. The attacker now holds a map the company itself may lack.
steps.defender: Outside-in inventory (ASM) plus DNS purge discipline removes exactly this raw material.

steps.title: Buy employee data
steps.caption: From a credential broker the operator buys leaked staff logins from an infostealer log. Four employees reused their corporate password.
steps.defender: Dark-web monitoring exists for this moment. Every corporate hit should force a reset - before the buyer logs in.

detection.detail: A weak signal exists but is not yet a confirmed alert.

steps.title: Pick the quiet entry
steps.caption: Comparing the map and the credentials, the operator chooses the legacy VPN portal: reachable, weakly monitored, one reused password away from a foothold.
steps.defender: MFA on every password portal kills this plan. Coverage must include legacy systems, not just the main ones.

detection.label: Alert raised
detection.detail: The SOC has enough evidence to open an incident.

steps.title: The SOC's blind spot
steps.caption: The SOC sees no packets and no logins - everything happened on vendor platforms. Only two indirect echoes exist: a vendor 'your brand was searched' notice and an unowned breach-monitor alert.
steps.defender: Your wins here are procedural: own the exposure queue, ingest vendor alerts, and rotate exposed credentials fast.
